newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain rate to end year at 4,0% - DWS.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain rate to end year at 4,0% - DWS.

text.p: German Investment trust DWS Deutsche Gesellschaft fur Wertpapiersparen mbH expects the Bank of Spain to cut its official rate by at least 200 basis points in 1997 because of pressure on the currency.
Therefore, despite a sharp decline in Spanish yields, it is still a good time to invest in the Spanish debt market, according to the bank.

"As it did last week, I expect the next step (for the Bank of Spain) in mid-February to be another 25 basis points," Ralf Schreyer of DWS, Deutsche Bank's AG German fund management unit, told reporters after a Euromoney conference here.
The Bank of Spain cut its official rate 25 basis points on January 16 to six percent.
Schreyer noted the big jump in the Bank of Spain's currency reserves during 1996 and said the central bank would not like further peseta strength.
"So, they either have to intervene in the foreign market or, more easily, to cut their official rate," he said.
He said Spain's key rate could end 1997 near 100 basis points over its German counterpart, which he expected to end the year unchanged at the current three percent.
He attributed the pressure on the peseta to the 200-plus basis point spread in cash yields between two-year Spanish Bonos and German Bunds.

"I expect the Bundesbank to stay at around three percent (until the end of the year) and Spain to end 100 basis point higher. Despite the fact they are saying they are looking at inflation of 2.6 percent, they would not have any problem," he said.
